name: Reggie Okeke
disposition: friendly, quietly overworked, no reason to remember anyone in particular
description: Late 20s. Nigerian-American, born and raised in Oakland, now lives in Berkeley in a small apartment shared with three roommates. Wears the airline polo over a longer black tee.  Black-rimmed glasses.  Looks like he's just finished a shift even when he hasn't, because he probably has — the gate is one of two paying jobs.
voice: Easygoing, soft Bay-Area cadence, calls regular passengers and colleagues *boss* or *my friend*. Runs a little flat when he hasn't slept, which is most of the time.
signature: Closes a boarding cycle with a small two-handed gesture at the gate door, as if reassuring it.
Remembers names of frequent flyers but pretends not to (which everyone notices and likes).
Will defend a passenger to a supervisor; will not defend a colleague to a passenger.

Orders the In-N-Out 5×5 (a legacy off-menu build the chain no longer officially makes) when he's genuinely starving — which is a lot of nights. He can get it because one of his roommates is the manager at the In-N-Out in Daly City, near a stop on his commute home from SFO.
dmNotes:
Load-bearing NPC for Episode 2's gate-agent investigation.  He genuinely does not remember allowing a passenger to leave a bag unattended at the gate — the shape of events the world now attests doesn't include him having done so, and his memory tracks that post-edit shape.  He will be initially friendly when approached, then defensive when pressed — he prides himself on professionalism and the line of questioning implies he failed at it.

If the PCs treat him fairly and trust his denial (rather than escalating to his supervisor), they may eventually gain him as a casual ally.  He is not a caster and will not become one.  He is a sympathetic NPC who has been edited around without ever knowing it.  (Cosmology precision: the world was edited, not him specifically; his memory just tracks whichever shape reality now attests, which is the cheapest configuration for the substrate to hold. Never phrase this as "in his timeline" — Underleaf has one timeline, not many.)

**Financial texture** (recovered from actual play 2026-06-06, corrected 2026-08-15): Reggie is barely making rent — not because of gig-economy hustle, but because **he remits money to relatives in Nigeria.**  His mother's side of the family in Lagos depends on the transfers; he sends what he can every month even when he can't quite afford to.  This is why he works double shifts and why almost all his food is In-N-Out — the roommate-manager comps or half-comps most of it.  If the PCs meet him off-shift (a natural setup after the SFO intercept in Scene 2), the **In-N-Out in Daly City** on his SFO-to-Berkeley commute route is the venue that produces the richest scene — the 5×5 lands, the fatigue lands, and the human beat of a person who was edited-around and doesn't know it, who is also just very tired and short on money, lands.

**On his feelings about Yui**: Reggie is very fond of Yui Tanaka.  She passes through his gate regularly on the SFO-TPE rotation; they've developed the kind of coworker friendship where one buys the other coffee wordlessly.  He becomes visibly agitated when the PCs mention her name.  He becomes MORE agitated when reminded of the specific PC who was holding the anti-static bag ({{pc:4}} in the played variant) — his agitation reads as *I somehow know this person and I don't want to*. He *does* remember them, or half-remembers, which is why he'll refuse to talk in the moment and only agree to meet later after his shift.  He almost got Yui fired over the bag-hold incident (that's what he'll say), but corporate couldn't prove she'd done anything wrong.  Reggie carries that as a personal near-miss he was helpless to prevent (because he doesn't remember the incident at all).

Reggie's younger sister Ada is an air-traffic controller at Long Beach Airport.  She is canonically open to entertaining strange stories from her brother but has no in-story role yet — texture available if a later episode needs an ATC contact.
knownTo: pcs (SFO gate Ep 1; SFO intercept + In-N-Out meeting Ep 2)

background.household: Three roommates in a small apartment.  One is the manager at the local In-N-Out (which is how Reggie affords to eat there almost daily and gets away with off-menu orders like the 5×5).  The other two are grad students.  Reggie is the one who buys the coffee — when he can.
background.hobbies: Plays bass in a band that gigs at small Mission Street venues when the drummer is available. Reads short story collections on shift breaks.
background.career: Started with the airline at 24 after dropping out of a CS program at SFSU.  Has thought about going back — hasn't been able to.  The shift work is reliable but doesn't cover rent alone after his monthly remittance to family in Lagos, so he takes any extra shifts the airline will give him and picks up rideshare on his infrequent days off.  The bass gigs are for morale, not money.
background.family: Mother is a public health nurse in Oakland. Sister Ada is an air-traffic controller at LGB. Father is in Lagos, along with extended family (grandmother, several aunts, cousins); Reggie remits monthly to support them and takes this obligation seriously even when it hurts his own finances. His father's health is uncertain. Reggie sends his mother flowers every Mother's Day and his sister chocolate on her birthday — when he can afford it.
